lines.text: Two real, independent sources on this exact mechanism agree, in their own words.
The broker assigns each producer a real id, and deduplicates by a real sequence number sent with every message.

So here's the real split this whole topic turns on: a broker's own promise about delivery and a consumer's own promise about effects are answering two completely different questions, and mixing them up is exactly where this kind of bug comes from.
A crash doesn't erase what already happened; it only erases the broker's own record of having heard about it, which is precisely why the work can come back around a second time looking brand new.
The fix was never about trying to stop that second arrival. It was about giving the consumer its own memory, so arriving twice and mattering twice stop being the same thing.
